  "text": "At closing time, Martin found a pair of glasses on the returns trolley. One arm had been repaired with green thread.

He carried them to the desk, where Ruth was counting the till.

“Anyone ask about these?”

She shook her head. “Put them in the drawer.”

The drawer held two gloves, several keys and a photograph nobody had claimed in eleven months.

Martin left the glasses on top.

On Thursday, an old woman came in carrying a book wrapped in a supermarket bag. She waited while he checked it through.

“My brother usually brings them,” she said.

Martin looked at the name on the screen. He knew her brother: a tall man who borrowed books about canals and always asked whether the heating was working.

“He’s not driving now,” she said.

“I think we have his glasses.”

He opened the drawer.

The woman took them but did not put them in her bag. She held them by the bridge, letting the arms hang open.

“I did that,” she said, touching the thread. “He wouldn’t let me buy him another pair.”

Martin slid the returned book onto the trolley.

“Would he like something else?”

“He’s finding it difficult to concentrate.”

They stood quietly for a moment. Behind her, the printer began feeding out paper.

“There are some with photographs,” Martin said.

He showed her the shelf. She chose a thin book about waterways, opening it first to check the size of the print.

At the desk, she tucked the glasses into her coat pocket.

“Three weeks?”

“Three weeks,” he said. “You can phone if you need longer.”"
